editorial:
Imagine you are desperate for a dream job, and the only thing standing in your way is a simple game of Simon Says. You are thrown into a room with three other strangers, and the stakes feel incredibly high. At first, the vibe is tense but professional, and you feel like if you just follow the instructions and stay focused, you will win. The characters are relatable people who have done everything right in their lives, making you root for them as they try to outsmart each other in this strange competition.

What really hits home is how the movie shows that the game is rigged from the start. The acting is great, and the pacing keeps you on the edge of your seat as the rules start to shift. While some parts feel a bit slow, the big reveals make it worth it. If you love stories about people fighting a broken system, you should definitely check this out. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out that the company never intended to hire based on skill. The game was designed to see who would break first or who would cheat. Even the winner realizes that the job is just another trap where they will be controlled. The final twist shows that the rules were fake, and the whole process was just a cruel way for the bosses to feel powerful over the applicants.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about corporate greed.
